Cascade releases from final versions. Trail #462. Worktree wp-cascade-fixpoint. Owner wants this fixed now. Background (session 2a2dd47e, on f5c770ca0): cascade severities raised against an intermediate aligned version are kept, so a consumer can be released with an unnecessary patch although the final versions already satisfy its range (example: released lib-a@1.0.0 and untagged lib-b@2.0.0 in one fixed group; a major on a-upstream cascades a patch to lib-b exposing 1.0.1, releasing its >=2.0.0 consumer; peer escalation then aligns the group to 2.0.0, which that consumer accepted). A filter after convergence is not enough: dropping a consumer can change group alignment and transitive dependents (cascade.rs: raise 587-608, group max-severity 290/361, aligned version 325-345/394-405, range pass 413-452, convergence_bound 679). Design: derive cascade-only releases as a fixpoint where severities can go down as well as up, recomputing from the explicit (changeset, inference, group) seeds each round. Before coding, write the termination argument in 3-5 lines in the PR body (for example a bounded descending chain, or iterate from the explicit-seed set and only add consumers whose ranges reject the current final targets, which is monotone). Keep ConvergedTargets as the one output. Tests first: the example above releases no consumer; a consumer outside its range still releases; transitive cascades and fixed/linked groups still align; existing cascade tests stay green. Mutants on the diff. Cap: if the production change exceeds about 200 lines or the argument doesn't hold, stop and report. Patch changeset for users (no more unnecessary patch releases of dependents). Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha). Be fast and lean; GitHub CI runs the full suite, so don't duplicate it.
- Read AGENTS.md. Prefer a type or private constructor over a check; delete checks a type makes redundant; fix sibling call sites in the same PR.
- A check, preview, dry run or test must run on exactly the structure the real path executes (one shared graph or derivation, the real tool), never a projection, copy or re-implementation. When fixing a failing or flaky test, assert the measured behaviour still happens.
- No new traits, async or frameworks. No new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead.
- Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main. Write the failing test first for behaviour changes.
- Local checks: `cargo test -p <touched crate>` and `just lint` (clippy) for the crates you touched; `just doc-check` if docs changed. Do not run local `just ci` or a fresh reviewer unless the lead asks; let GitHub CI do the full run.
- If you change a public signature in callisto-manifests or callisto-model, also run `just fuzz-check` (the fuzz crate is outside the workspace, so crate tests miss it).
- Run `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` only for new decision logic, not for merges, renames, docs, CI or tests; never commit mutants.out*.
- Merges and conflict resolutions: resolve, run the touched crate's tests, push. Nothing else.
- Changeset (`cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add ...`) only for user-visible changes, written for users.
- Signed commits, no session trailer. Merge the latest origin/main right before pushing (no rebase, no force-push). Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link the given trail, open with entire trail ci-pr.
- Trails are semantic outcomes shared by many PRs. Never change a trail's title or description (no `entire trail update` on it, no `entire trail create` to rename it). Put PR-specific text in the PR body with `gh pr edit <n> --body-file`. Link your branch to the trail the lead named; if your work does not fit that trail's outcome, ask the lead instead of linking it anyway.
- If CI fails, fix that failure only. If Entire raises findings, fix only wrong results, broken recovery, security issues or checks that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead.
- Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what you ran.
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.

## Two phases

| Phase | Entry point | Touches disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan | `commands::plan_version` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs`) returns a `VersionPlan` | No |
| Apply | `apply_version_plan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`) | Yes; takes `&ApplyPermit` |

- `VersionPlan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs`) is the whole change: bumps, dependency spec rewrites, platform manifest writes, owner `optionalDependencies` pins, changelog sections, consumed changesets, `pre.json` updates and diagnostics. It is in memory only (no `Serialize`).
- Dependency range rewrites and E319 take a target only from `ConvergedTargets` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade/converged.rs`). Only `cascade.rs` builds it: `solve_cascade` once group alignment stops moving targets, and `snapshot_rewrites` from the snapshot versions.
- A changelog section is `## {version}`, a date and compare-link line, then Major, Minor and Patch Changes groups (`[changelog] layout = "grouped"`, the default), or the heading and one bullet list (`"flat"`). `render_section` is pure: the planner puts the layout, the UTC date and the link in `ChangelogInput::style`, and the link needs a GitHub repository (`[release] forge-repository`, else the `origin` remote) plus a tag on the previous version. Readers (`find_section`, `has_heading`, release notes) key on the `## {version}` line only, so they read both layouts; a fixed group's release notes file each member's entries under the bump group the member recorded them in.
- `plan_version` is shared: `version`, `status`, `compose-pr-body` and `release plan --package` all compute the same plan.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/markdown/` is the only place Markdown is scanned: fenced code, ATX headings, heading rebase, the headline split and `Breaking:`/`Action:` markers (`markers.rs`). A new pass asks those questions there and joins `corpus.rs`; it does not write its own line scanner.
- `ReleasePreview` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/release_preview.rs`) is the serializable, versioned view of a plan for people: packages, merged changes, bystanders and findings. Surfaces such as the PR body render it; they do not recompute from the plan. `version --emit-preview` writes it before apply consumes the changesets, and `compose-pr-body --preview` renders from that file. Each changeset change records `pr`, the pull request that added it, read from the first-parent merge commits in one `git log` when the history names one. `ReleasePreview` also carries findings from the changesets (a `Breaking:` or `Action:` marker, a breaking marker whose bump is too low, and no \"backward compatible\" claim when there is a breaking one) and `unreleased`, the publishable packages with source changes since their last tag that the plan does not bump (a package with no tag has no baseline and is not listed) (`version --emit-preview` computes it; a failure to look is a warning). `pr_labels()` derives the managed label catalog, with an `applied` flag per label, from the same findings. `--publish-plan` adds `publish`, the outcome of `plan_workspace_release_offline` on the versioned tree for exactly the packages the preview bumps (the committed decision holds those, not every unreleased package). It never observes a registry or the forge, so the checks that need one (a published version left behind, a name another project owns) are left to the release itself; a refusal becomes a `Stop` finding. `publish.versionedOnly` (optional, absent when empty) names the bumped packages with no publish target, such as a private fixed-group member, which are versioned but never published; the PR body lists them after the publish table. Rows are keyed by the qualified release identity, so `cargo/x` and `npm/x` stay apart.
- `changed_source_files_since_last_tag` lists, per package, the files that differ from its last tag after dropping `DEFAULT_IGNORED_PATHS` (tests, benches, examples, snapshots, Markdown), and `uncovered_changes` returns the changed packages that no pending changeset, nor any member of their fixed or linked group, covers. `unreleased_changes` builds `ReleasePreview.unreleased` from them, so the PR body lists the packages they find.
- A dry run never gets a permit, so it reports the plan and never calls apply.
- `snapshot` applies with `ApplyOptions::transient`: manifests are written, while changelogs, changeset deletion and git staging are skipped.

A crash or a failed lockfile refresh can stop apply after some files are written. Applying the same plan again is file-level idempotent, and a fresh run recovers that plan from a checkpoint ([ADR 13](../adr/0013-interrupted-version-runs-resume-from-a-checkpoint-ref.md)):

A dependent is released only when its range rejects the version its dependency is finally released at. Before, a cascade raise computed against an intermediate group-aligned version was kept even after the group moved past it.

Example (tested): released `lib-a@1.0.0` and untagged `lib-b@2.0.0` in one fixed group. A major on `a-upstream` cascades a patch to `lib-b`, exposing 1.0.1, which a `>=2.0.0` consumer rejects. A transitive peer escalation then aligns the group to 2.0.0, which the consumer accepts. That consumer is no longer released.

## Design

`solve_cascade` now iterates rounds. Each round:

1. starts from the explicit seeds (changesets and inference) plus the cascade raises the previous round required,
2. computes targets and aligns linked and fixed groups (the existing group passes, moved unchanged into `settle_round`),
3. derives the raise each consumer needs from those settled targets (`required_raises`).

It stops when a round requires exactly the raises it started from. `ConvergedTargets` stays the one output, and the rewrite and floor-raise passes run on it unchanged. The old provisional worklist and `raise` are deleted.

## Termination

- Rounds 1..n (n = package count) use the required raises as they are, so a raise can be dropped. An acyclic chain is discovered one hop per round and settles within n rounds.
- From round n+1 on, each round keeps the previous raise when it is at least as high as the newly required one (pointwise max). The raise map then only grows: at most n consumers, each raised at most three times (patch, minor, major), so at most 3n further rounds before a round adds nothing.
- Total rounds are at most n + 3n + 1 = 4n + 1, the existing `convergence_bound`. Exceeding it still returns `CascadeNotConverged` (E105).
- Either stop is sound: the final round's required raises are at most the applied ones, so every consumer whose range rejects a final target is released. In the first phase it is exact: every cascade release is justified by a final target.

## Tests

- The example above releases no consumer; with a `^1.0.0` range the consumer is released, its reason names lib-b at 2.0.0.
- A transitive chain releases every consumer; a seed's own changeset reason survives an equal cascade raise.
- The bound test also checks a cascade that needs exactly the bound's one round succeeds.
- Existing cascade, fixed and linked group tests unchanged and green.

## Checks run

- `cargo test -p callisto-graph`: all pass except `registry_argv::a_standalone_root_package_packs_and_publishes_as_a_tarball_without_a_workspace_flag`, which fails locally only because the sandbox denies npm's cache under `~/.npm`; CI runs it.
- `just lint`, `just doc-check`: pass.
- `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` on `cascade.rs`: 13 targeted survivors now caught. Remaining misses: two `> to >=` in the moved group passes (equivalent: re-inserts the same max), the tie-break `>` in `required_raises` (first equal edge vs last), and the union-phase switch and merge comparisons, which only matter for workspaces that do not settle in n rounds.
- Not run: `just ci`, `just fuzz-check` (no public signature changed in callisto-model or callisto-manifests), `just bench`.

Spec `VER-CAS-01` and `docs/architecture/versioning.md` updated. Patch changeset for `callisto-cli`.

I did both things the lead asked for, and PR #637 is updated on `wp-cascade-fixpoint` at `a345b67`. GitHub reports the commit signature as `valid`. origin/main hadn't moved, so no merge was needed.

**1. Bench (500-package shapes).** `version --dry-run` is no slower and starts the same number of git processes:

| workspace | before (ms) | after (ms) | git processes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| cargo | 423 | 425 | 16 / 16 |
| pnpm | 446 | 422 | 16 / 16 |
| foreign tags | 373 | 376 | 27 / 27 |

These shapes don't really test the change. They only add patch changesets that dependents' caret ranges already accept, so the cascade finishes in one round.

I timed a worst case separately: a 500-package chain where each package pins the next with `=1.0.0`, and the last one gets a major. The cascade goes from 1.2 ms to 109 ms. The cause is that each round reaches one more package down the chain and recomputes everything already released, so cost grows with chain depth times released packages. For a chain 10 deep I estimate about 2 ms; I didn't measure that. I left it unoptimised. Making it fast would mean an incremental worklist, which I've offered to the lead.

**2. Test for the keep-only rounds.** The test fixture now lets the test list fewer packages, which forces the solver into the rounds that only keep bumps:
- With 3 packages listed, the unneeded bump on the consumer is still dropped.
- With 2 listed, it is kept, and its reason names the released 2.0.0.
- A second test checks that a bump kept at major isn't lowered later by a minor requirement.

All 11 mutants on those lines are now caught. The only misses left in the file are three with no real effect: two in the group-alignment code I moved, and the choice between two equally severe edges.

**Checks:** `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib cascade`, `just lint`, `cargo mutants` limited to those lines, and `cargo bench` before and after all passed. I did not run `just ci`. The PR body now has the bench table, the worst-case timing and the updated mutants results. I've sent the lead a short report.
